props.title: How Solar Panels Work
props.subtitle: From a ray of sunlight to the socket in your wall

scenes.narration: Every hour, enough sunlight hits the Earth to power the planet for a year. So how do we catch it?

props.title: Why solar matters
items: No fuel to burn, so no smoke or carbon
Works on rooftops, fields and even satellites
Now one of the cheapest kinds of electricity

scenes.narration: Solar burns no fuel, panels last decades, they work almost anywhere, and today they are one of the cheapest ways to make power.
Light strikes the panel, which makes direct current. An inverter turns it into the alternating current your home uses, and any extra flows to the grid.

right.title: Coal
points: Fuel must be mined and shipped

scenes.narration: Compared with coal, solar needs no fuel and makes no smoke, but it only works while the sun is shining.

props.label: of sunlight reaches the Earth
props.context: About ten thousand times all the energy humanity uses

scenes.narration: About one hundred seventy three thousand terawatts of sunlight reach us, thousands of times what we use.
Inside each cell, light hits silicon, knocks electrons free, and metal contacts collect them as a current we can use.
Since twenty ten, the price of a solar module has fallen by more than ninety percent.

props.text: I'd put my money on the sun and solar energy. What a source of power!

scenes.narration: Nearly a century ago, Thomas Edison already said he would put his money on the sun.

props.title: Quick recap
points: Sunlight frees electrons in silicon cells
The panel makes DC, the inverter makes AC
Extra power can flow back to the grid
Solar has become cheap and clean

scenes.narration: So: light frees electrons, the inverter makes usable power, extra goes to the grid, and it keeps getting cheaper.
